To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have used a novel strategy to identify genes that are differentially regulated during metastatic colonization and we have shown that these genes are correlated with metastatic progression in patient-derived data.
we used a novel microarray-based approach to identify a cohort of genes whose transcription is dynamically altered during the course of metastasis formation.
the majority of genes identified as being differentially expressed during the timecourse were downregulated in cells expressing ectopic MKK.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying and characterizing the molecular and cellular events associated with metastatic colonization.
the identification of genes whose expression is altered in MKK4-overexpressing metastasis-suppressed SKOV3ip1 human ovarian cancer cell lines.
understanding the cellular and molecular mechanisms by which metastatic cancer cells colonize distant organs and tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our data support the hypothesis that MKK4 suppresses metastatic colonization by regulating a transcriptional program that is associated with cell proliferation and cell adhesion.
the MKK4 suppressor gene has been shown to inhibit the metastatic colonization of SKOV3ip cells in the peritoneal cavity, which is a clinically relevant model for human epithelial ovarian cancer.
MKK4 expression during the timecourse in vivo suppresses omental metastatic colonizing ability of ovarian cancer cells, in part, through repression of the genes that were identified.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

MKK4-mediated suppression of ovarian cancer omental metastasis is associated with a time-dependent shift in transcriptional programs that are involved in cytokinesis, cytoplasmic remodeling, and cell motility, and this is associated with a shift in the expression of genes that are involved in metastasis in patients.
the transcriptional profile of SKOV3ip1 cells is altered in a time-dependent manner in response to MKK4 expression, and these changes are associated with a reduction in metastatic colonization.
MKK4 suppresses metastatic colonization by modulating a dynamic program of transcriptional changes that are associated with cell proliferation and cell adhesion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transcriptional changes that occur during the early stages of metastatic colonization are critical to the establishment of a successful metastasis.
the transcriptional signature associated with metastatic colonization is highly dynamic.
metastatic colonization is a dynamic process that involves a complex interplay between the cancer cell and the microenvironment.
